subject: Pathology
summary: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) measures the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. A prolonged APTT suggests factor deficiencies, inhibitors, or lupus anticoagulant, guiding further work‑up and treatment.

sections.p: APTT is a plasma clotting test that evaluates the intrinsic pathway (factors XII, XI, IX, VIII) and the common pathway (factors X, V, II, fibrinogen). It is performed after adding phospholipid and a contact activator to patient plasma.
b: Used to screen for hemophilia, lupus anticoagulant, and monitor heparin therapy

t.b: Prolonged APTT indicates a deficiency or inhibitor in intrinsic/common pathway.
Identifies specific hemophilia or acquired deficiency.
Correction suggests factor deficiency; no correction suggests inhibitor.

sections.p: APTT itself is not staged, but the underlying disorder is. For hemophilia, severity is classified by factor activity: mild (>5–40%), moderate (1–5%), severe (<1%).
b: Severe hemophilia presents with spontaneous bleeding; mild often asymptomatic.

sections.p: The most common causes of a prolonged APTT are factor deficiencies, lupus anticoagulant, and heparin therapy. In low‑resource settings, infections and herbal remedies can also interfere.
b: Vitamin K deficiency (rare, usually prolongs PT)

sections.p: Patients with factor deficiencies may have bruising, joint bleeds, or prolonged bleeding after surgery. Lupus anticoagulant patients often have thrombosis rather than bleeding.
b: Prolonged bleeding after trauma or surgery

sections.p: APTT is the first test; if abnormal, a systematic work‑up follows to identify the cause.
A prolonged APTT can mask a bleeding risk or, if due to lupus anticoagulant, predispose to life‑threatening clots.
b: Unprovoked deep vein thrombosis or stroke

sections.p: Treat the underlying cause, provide supportive care, and monitor coagulation status. Anticoagulation is avoided if a bleeding disorder is present.
b: Factor replacement (VIII or IX concentrates) for hemophilia

t.b: Specific factor to replace the deficient protein.
Only if deficiency suspected; usually normal in intrinsic pathway.
Risk of severe bleeding outweighs benefit in factor deficiency.
If accidental heparin exposure causes dangerous prolongation.

sections.p: Regular monitoring of factor levels and APTT ensures adequate protection. Vaccination against hepatitis B and safe injection practices reduce infection‑related coagulopathies.
b: Annual factor level checks for hemophilia patients

sections.p: APTT is often mistaken for PT/INR, which assess the extrinsic pathway. A normal PT with prolonged APTT points to intrinsic pathway issues.

whenToSeekHelp: Pregnancy loss in a woman with prolonged APTT

faq.q: What does a normal APTT mean?
faq.a: It indicates that the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways are functioning normally.

faq.q: Can APTT be prolonged by vitamin K deficiency?
faq.a: No, vitamin K deficiency mainly prolongs PT/INR.

faq.q: Why is a mixing study performed?
faq.a: It distinguishes between a factor deficiency and an inhibitor.

exam: Explain why a patient with hemophilia A has a prolonged APTT but normal PT.
Describe the steps you would take if a patient on heparin develops a prolonged APTT.
Interpret a mixing study that does not correct the prolonged APTT.
